Filmed so beautifully. Best thing about it. Soundtrack was subpar, but I guess it was up to snuff at the time. Now the issues. Why the fuck was Scottie so hung up on the fact that Madeline was pressured into being an accomplice to a murder? Like it seemed like she was being manipulated against her will into that, yet the love she felt for Scottie was real. After the twist reveal that it was the real wife’s body thrown from the tower, it was such a garbage plot. They could have had everything they wanted, especially Scottie. He should have been happy to find out that Judy was really Madeline no? And then at the end when the nun scares Judy and causes her to fall? I mean commmee on!? If you’re gonna have something like that be the ending, at least make it Midge that pushes her out of jealousy. What was even the point of Midge at all if not to build up to something like that

Really bad dude. 😭 Surprisingly bland and stupid. My rating genuinely started at 3.5 stars and steadily worked its way down to 1 and even that feels generous. Truly was expecting something brilliant. Hell of a lot of filler and needless repetition. And it drags so much then packs too much into the end and ts just goes “the end!!!”. None of it is really believable or meaningful, it’s all very forced 🚨to me🚨 The score is also irritating eventually. I have trouble caring about any of the characters in any capacity whatsoever. They’re not cool or likeable or honorable, except for midge the goat (of course I’m not saying “characters in movies must be good or else movie bad”, I am saying that it’s nice to care about the characters a little at the very least lmaooo.) Just so bland. And Scottie is a damn creep dude. He sucks ass and genuinely becomes a disgusting, scary person. Hate that mf. The scene in the clothing store of broke my heart. Judy pmo she shoulda kicked him in the balls A personal “flaw” of mine is that I kind of hate the acting in movies of this age. It’s like I’m watching people try their hardest to “really act”. Always makes me cringe. Anyway it is undeniably stunning visually. Gorgeous film. Brilliant colors, especially the greens. So pretty.

vou dizer isto com todo o respeito, mas que seca do caraças. eu sinto me sempre um bocado mal por criticar um clássico, como se tivesse a ofender a Mona Lisa ou assim, mas isto não tinha ponta por onde se lhe pegasse. eu ontem adormeci a ver a primeira parte do filme e depois pensei “okay há de melhorar”, só que o tempo foi passando e só PIOROU. no início o pace é extremamente lento e não acontece praticamente nada, e no final é igual ao início. o verdadeiro suspense era quando é que esta porcaria terminava. e depois para melhorar o final também foi péssimo. sinceramente se não tivesse começado pelo Psycho acho que não tinha visto mais nenhum filme do Hitchcock. hoje estive com a minha avó e estivemos a refletir sobre como estes clássicos foram revolucionários na altura, e como tanto a linguagem como a definição do que era o “suspense” mudou drasticamente, massss ela não se lembrar de ter visto o Vertigo devia ter sido mais um dos imensos sinais de que isto não se ia compor. não sei bem, talvez não seja cinéfila o suficiente para apreciar isto, ou secalhar não percebi bem o plot (impossível). o Senhor Hitchcock que se inspire no filme e assombre-me a mim também pelo que eu escrevi. por mim, desde que não tenha de voltar a ver isto, está tudo bem.

من الأفلام التي كنت متشوق جدا لمشاهدتها ، كان لدي شعور غريب إنني سأحب العمل، لكن طوال مدة الفيلم لم انجذب لا للسيناريو ولا للحبكة، الفيلم عظيم ؟ ، بالنسبة للكثيرين نعم ولكن بالنسبة لي ضحية توقعات عالية. قصة الفيلم بلا حرق احداث : شرطي متقاعد بسبب فوبيا المرتفعات، لكنه يكلف بمهمة لمراقبة امرأة ذي تصرفات غريبة، مع مرور الوقت يكتشف اشيار غريبة عن تلك المرأة تجعله يشك بها ويحبها ويقع بحبها بنفس الوقت. رأيي بالفيلم: لمدة ساعة كاملة وانا انتظر بداية الأحداث، وعندما بدأت الأحداث تصبح اكثر إثارة لم اشعر انني مهتم او منسجم. افضل ما بالفيلم هو الموسيقى و المشاهد التصويرية. حبكة الفيلم بالكامل مبنية على خدعة ، وعندما تم الكشف عنها خلال الفيلم لم تحدث المفاجئة او الصدمة. الخوف من المرتفعات والشعور بالدوار شيء اساسي للشخصية، حتى انه كان محرك مهم بحدث ما بالفيلم. انا غير مهتم بالسيناريو ولم انجذب له وبالتالي كل ما حدث بالفيلم من مشاهد واحداث لم يقدم لي شيء حتى الاداءات التمثيلية كانت بطابع مسرحي، لذا ببساطة لن احاول ان اقلل من الفيلم وكأنني ناقد سينمائي يفهم التفاصيل وكلامه الصح. باختصار هذا رأي متابع عادي

“Here I was born, and there I died. It was only a moment for you; you took no notice.” As someone who has previously enjoyed each Hitchcock film I’ve been exposed too, I genuinely cannot bring myself to understand why this is so hyped. All the praise I see for this has to do with the symbolism and metaphors but can we talk about the actual narrative for a second? The plot here is one of the most contrived stories I’ve ever seen in a film, attempting to do way too much yet never taking the time to fully commit. Madeline is compelling for the first half but once the second half starts she doesn’t matter because the “character” isn’t real; Judy however is, but you don’t care to root for her because she’s an accomplice to murder and in love with the most mediocre man ever. Speaking of which: Scottie is such a boring main character. He’s a terrible PI who doesn’t get caught only because the person he’s following knows he’s there, he’s incredibly abusive to Judy prior him figuring out who she really is (No, grief is not an excuse), and ultimately he also just has an affair with whom he believes to be a married woman. My point is: none of the character are compelling or root-able by the end except for Midge, but the movie forgets about her even being a character following the second act. I get this is a very internal film from Hitchcock, but that doesn’t mean it’s a good movie. Yes the color, editing, and sound are great; but what I value most is narrative and this narrative is awfully paced with an abysmal payoff. I know this is going to go become one of my certified hot takes but I’ve gotta stand on business. Hitchcock is still on my Mount Rushmore of horror directors. But if you want to be an honest critic (even just for fun on Letterboxd), you gotta not just glaze everything a great director puts out. This wasn’t received well when it came out and I can see why. Is Hitchcock still a certified master? Yes. Do I still think this movie is kind of a narrative shitfest? Also yes.

Hitchcock sabe construir tensão e criar imagens absurdamente marcantes, mas, no fim, a história não conseguiu me prender tanto quanto eu esperava. E aquele final??? Simplesmente não gostei. 🫠 Depois de toda a construção, achei que o desfecho me deixou mais frustrada do que impactada. Não esperava este desfecho mais ou menos de um diretor como o Hitchcock. Reconheço demais a importância do filme e a qualidade visual, mas acho que Vertigo simplesmente não funcionou pra mim. Bonito de assistir, mas não me pegou.
I get the appeal for the most part, but there are aspects of the story that just haven’t aged super well, imo. Very filmic and beautiful to look at. Rear Window is better.

Hay muchos elementos que me disgustan de la cinta, siento que la trama pasa de un género a otro de una manera muy abrupta comenzamos con una especie de misterio que tienes ciertas cosas interesantes, después evidenciamos las secuelas que el protagonista posee a raiz de su miedo a las alturas su Vértigo y por ultimo una especie de romance con comportamientos obsesivos; siento que al añadir tantas cosas a la película hace que estos mismos aspectos se descuiden, el misterio que es lo primero que nos dan a conocer es de las cosas más flojas en consideración mia. Esto no quita el hecho de que la forma de grabar, las técnicas implementadas, junto a varias secuencias y planos son bastante impresionantes y memorables, teniendo en cuenta la antigüedad de la cinta

I understand why this film is considered a classic and why it's popular but it's not for me. I found Alfred Hitchcock’s use of dolly zooms, slow and quiet scenes and color was a really unique and cool way of conveying confusion and the “vertigo effect”. Some scenes were put in a first person perspective of Scottie when he's experiencing acrophobia and there's a dolly zoom going downward. I thought this was really interesting because it lets the viewer experience this with him instead of just watching, I thought this fit really well with the whole disorienting and spiraling themes of the movie. Another thing Hitchcock did in Vertigo that was impressive to me was his use of color. When Scottie first spots Madeleine in the restaurant, she's wearing bright green and the background is a really bright red/pink, It's all so vibrant and surreal so I thought again this really fits that whole confusing vibe of everything But, nevermind how pretty the shots were, the coloring and cinematography just wasn't enough to keep me fully engaged with this film. The pacing got kind of unbearable after a while, the whole sequence of Scottie following Madeleine while she wandered around, and following her as she drove I thought went on for a little too long. So, overall I get why Vertigo is so well liked but personally I wouldn't watch this again.

Vertigo has been considered one of the best movies that you can view in your life. From the different camera movements and scenes, this movie establishes the difference between obsession and what is true to life. The film starts out with a vibrant array of colors, ranging on the full color spectrum. This reveals a brighter mood at the beginning of the film and creates the illusion that everything is alright. The colors in the film later will introduce red and green tints that respectivly represent danger and mystery. One example of this is the hotel scene where the hotel sign shines into the room while you wonder if it actually is madaline. With the hair being the origional color and her wearing the same suit you can see that it actualy is madaline. We can also see the danger happen while detective is having the dream and can see what madaline has seen in the past when she was going "crazy". Theere is also the theme of obsession and creating an image of someone that they cannot live up to. We can see when Madaline supposidly dies that the detective is completley broken down and cannot function as he always has since he was in love. This then over time creates the image of Madaline as she once was and when he meets her again as a different person, he cannot be content of who she is now and needs to change her to what he has envisioned. I feel that this film really challenged me to sit through it and really focus on whwat is actually happening. I feel that movies need a concrete plot and I feel that the story has to be known to the watcher. In conclusion I feel that this film deserves the rating that I gave it because of the story it had and not the cinematography or the score.

Movie was boring and I don't like it. I do However have somethings I do like about this film. I like the stunning visuals in the film which surprised me for a film that rebased in 1958. The colors really pop in this movie. It has very good use of composition that makes many frames that can become good photos if paused. The use of lighting in the movie was also spectacular. I especially like the shot of Judy in the dark with a green light showing on her. The room is dark so half of her face is blocked out by shadow and only a silloute of her face appears which looks very close to Madelines face. It gives hints on the truth of everything that happened which I will give points for. The themes of red and green  are also great with red representing violence, lust and passion and green representing death and sickness in both body and mind. The use of green also reminds me of Persona 3. Green is seen a lot in the dark hour and Tartarus. Other than that everything about this movie is something I feel like I won't want to experience again. The movie to slow of a pace for me in a bad way. I felt like I was fighting to stay awake during the movie. I think this film can be considered a classic because it is a good movie that doesn't appeal to me but would appeal to other people.

While it is well-made, the characters are not people I want to spend time with at all.  I admire the craft, but the story and the attempts at humor just feel forced and flat to me.  Every time I give this movie another chance hoping to proven wrong, I just end up walking away liking it a little less.  Jimmy Stewart is hard not to like and I completely understand his weird journey, I just don't enjoy it however.  I get none of the feelings I get when watching other Hitchcock movies.  Anymore, I just end up rooting against him and Kim Novak and wishing they both would just walk away from each other in the middle of the story. The cinematography and music however are not at fault here.  Again, it is a masterclass in how to make a movie look and sound great using all of the powers available at the time.  In that respect, it is one of Hitchcock's most impressive looking movies.  I just hate the story and characters.

i’m really struggling here. on the one hand, James Stewart is incredible. his character does it all as far as the emotional gamut, and is complicated and nuanced. i’m all there on that front. also, SF has never looked better. Midge’s office view of Russian Hill is stunning. Ernie’s is a place i wanna be. colors pop ooh ahh. on the other (more heavy) hand, the story is not all that complex, and quite frankly blows in the third act. i don’t buy the love story at all. and the Judy character is never credible at any point, to the point that I questioned if I was missing something for the last 30 minuets or so of the runtime. if the ending was a twist, it was hiding in plain sight. i really wish i connected with this “classic” more, and maybe after diving further into Hitchcock i will, but for the time being, this didn’t click and was a dud. will circle back.

I jumped at the opportunity to see a Hitchcock that I'd never seen before at one of my local cinemas. I love 'Rope' and 'Rear Window', so hearing that 'Vertigo' is one of Hitchcock's masterpieces seemed like a no-brainer. To discover that it's actually one of most overrated films ever made was a bit upsetting to say the least. We all left the cinema with a sour taste in our mouths, wishing we could get out $16 back and that someone had told us the truth: 'Vertigo' actually kind of sucks. Hitchcock: the master of suspense. Little to no suspense in the whole film. What makes many of his other films great is that we as the audience know things that the characters don't. Never the case here. The pacing? Painfully slow and borderline unengaging. The twist was apparent from halfway through the film, so the second half was just enduring one sad and tiresome display of misogyny after another. How Jimmy Stewart became such a popular heart-throb in the 40s-60s is beyond me. He just mostly plays unlikable assholes that somehow women still like. Plenty of people seem to say how gorgeous this film looks as well. The depiction of San Francisco, the bright colours, and the one major dream sequence stand out of bold and expressive. Yet, so much of the film is also filmed in bland locations, with uninspired set-pieces and straight-forward blocking. I wasn't nearly as impressed as I expected to be. Then, to wrap everything up. The ending is terrible, with no sense of mystery or closure to hold onto, just a sad dead-end with no real enjoyment or satisfaction. The entire second half is a painful ordeal. It's hard to believe I watched the same film that hundreds of thousands of men and women over the last 58 years have given 8/10, 9/10, or 10/10 reviews to, or called Hitchcock's masterpiece. A predictable, slow, stale, offensive and mostly just off-putting drag. Sad. 4/10

Letterboxd Film Gecesi #2 Bu etkinlik filmini @Beril ve @Yunus ile beraber izlemek nasip oldu. Eşlik ettikleri için teşekkür ederimm 🙏🏻 ----------------------------------------------------------- Vertigo'yu büyük bir merakla, sinema tarihinin en iyi filmlerinden biri diye övülmesine güvenerek ve beklentimi oldukça yüksek tutarak izledim ama dürüst olmak gerekirse tam sevemedim ya. Gerçekten baştan sona sevmeye çalıştım, şans vermeye çalıştım, ama maalesef olmadı. :( ----------------------------------------------------------- Ancak filmi tamamen kötüleyip hakkını asla yiyemem. Dönemine göre gerçekten çok iyi. Alfred Hitchcock'un o dönem için bulduğu kamera teknikleri, merdiven sahnelerindeki Vertigo efektleri sinematografik açıdan gerçekten başarılı, bunları beğendim. Atmosferi ve filmin renk paleti de göze güzel geliyor ama bir filmi sadece tekniği iyi diye baştan sona sevemiyorum maalesef. ----------------------------------------------------------- Benim için en büyük problem hikayenin ilerleyişi ve karakterlerin aşırı yapay durması oldu. Film o kadar yavaş ve hantal ilerliyor ki bir noktadan sonra ekrana bakarken daraldım. Tempoyu bir türlü ayarlayamamışlar. Scottie karakterinin Madeleine'e olan takıntısı, kadını takip ettiği sahneler beni içine çekmek yerine inanılmaz sıktı. ----------------------------------------------------------- Hadi ilk yarıyı gizem unsuru hatırına sabrederek izledim diyelim, ama ikinci yarıda hikayenin bağlandığı yer ve Scottie'nin Judy'yi zorla Madeleine'e dönüştürmeye çalıştığı sahneler beni filmden tamamen kopardı. Bir insanın bu kadar hastalıklı bir takıntıya sahip olması psikolojik bir öge olarak sunulmuş evet ama izlerken karakterle hiçbir şekilde empati kuramadım, aksine Scottie'den iyice irite oldum. ----------------------------------------------------------- Filmin sonundaki büyük ters köşe ve final sahnesi ise aşırı hızlı ve aceleye getirilmiş, birşey anlayamadan bir anda bitti film. He bu filmin sevenlerine ve klasik sinemaya saygım sonsuz tabii ki, bunlara asla lafım yok ama senaryonun bu kadar abartılmasını ve bu filmin gelmiş geçmiş en iyi yapımlardan biri olarak gösterilmesini gerçekten anlayamadım. Benim için bir kere izleyip geçilecek, bir daha da yüzüne bakmayacağım ortalama bir deneyimdi açıkçası. gokgok123

letterboxd film gecesi #2 Vertigo çıktığı dönem için belki harika ve devrimsel bir yapım olabilir ama sıradan bir izleyici olarak bugün için fazla standart buldum. Film boyunca hep bir odaksızlık var gibi geldi. Ne anlatılmak istenildiğine tam karar verilememiş gibi. Karakter ilişkilerinin yapay kurulması, olay örgüsünde hikayeye katkı sağlamayan kısımların olması hatta bazı karakterlerin senaryoda adeta konu mankenleri gibi işlevsiz olmaları gözüme fazla battı. Bir yerden sonra bu filmi ciddiye alarak izlememem gerekiyor herhalde diye düşünmeye bile başladım. Final de bu tezimi neredeyse doğrulacak kadar saçmaydı. Ayrıca filmin ismi neden Vertigo? Karakterin hasta olmasının tam olarak nasıl bir katkısı var? Filmin isminde, afişinde, introsunda bu kadar göze sokulunca merkezde bu konu olacak sandım. Halbuki karakter hiç hasta olmasa dahi ufak değişikliklerle bu açık kapatılabilirdi. James Stewart da artık sadece iki kez karşılaştığı kadınlara zil zurna aşık olmasın artık 🙏

Me resulta interesante que para la época Alfred Hitchcock haya utilizado la técnica “dolly zoom” para simular visualmente la acrofobia del prota, se vería más bacan en pantalla grande pero como vi en cuevana a 720p ni modo. La entrega no solo representa el vértigo sino que intenta crear una sensación de caer al abismo a través de la psique fracturada. Es asi que Scottie se obsesiona y entra en una espiral hacia su parte más retorcida que distorciona su concepto de amor por la obsesión del fantasma de una mujer casada que esta tratando de resucitar debido a su propia culpa. Y no es que la este reviviendo, mas bien manipula a la novia que conoce después para que sea igual a la otra mujer. La historia es interesante pero no me enganchó lo suficiente para permanecer atenta a todo, pienso que pudo durar menos; con respecto a las actuaciones y planos de cámara son buenas, pero no se esforzaron en el soundrack, lamentable.

Estadounidenses Não Sabem Beijar Nem mesmo a direção de Alfred Hitchcock foi suficiente para fazer o roteiro de Alec Coppel e Samuel A. Taylor resultar em um bom filme. A Midge (Bárbara Abel Geddes) é o maior exemplo da baixa qualidade do roteiro, porque ela é inútil na trama e desenvolvimento das demais personagens. A fotografia de Robert Burks é incrível, porque ele criou cenas lindas que complementaram a trama com mais camadas, um trabalho ímpar. Que mel é esse que o Scottie (James Stewart) tem? Um velho feio e desprezível desses. Dito isso, gosto muito como o filme muda nossa percepção sobre ele aos poucos. Hitchcock é um excelente diretor, porém a obra ser teatral, e depender muito disso para funcionar fez com que a imersão nunca fosse completa, principalmente porque tal teatralidade fazia os personagens se manterem nos mesmos ambientes quando não fazia sentido. Eu esperava muito mais desse que é um dos, se não o maior clássico do cinema. Esse é um dos poucos casos em que eu acho que uma nova adaptação de um filme seria bem-vinda.

Je suis franchement déçu par Vertigo. Je comprends totalement pourquoi le film est considéré comme un classique et je reconnais le talent d’Hitchcock dans la mise en scène, la photographie et l’ambiance, mais je n’ai jamais vraiment accroché. J’ai trouvé le film beaucoup trop lent et j’ai souvent eu l’impression qu’il ne se passait pas grand-chose. Le vertige de Scottie, qui semblait être un élément central au début, m’a finalement paru assez peu exploité. L’idée autour de Madeleine/Judy et l’obsession de Scottie sont intéressantes, surtout quand on comprend toute la manipulation, mais ça n’a pas suffi à me faire apprécier le film. Même la révélation finale m’a laissé assez froid. Je reconnais son importance et ses qualités cinématographiques, mais personnellement, je n’ai pas pris le plaisir que j’espérais devant ce film. Peut-être que je l’apprécierai davantage avec le temps, mais pour l’instant, grosse déception.

Vertigo has everything you expect from an old, classic film from the 50s or 60s. Stupid driving scenes, funny accents, and just the fact that it is weird overall. I wasn't expecting the film to go in the direction it did. For some reason, I thought it was going to be a bit more mind bending, but it really wasn't. I do have to say, I didn't see the twist at the end coming at all, but I wasn't really crazy impressed with it. It seemed kind of outlandish and unnecessary. I also thought it was weird how it was revealed. Hitchcock decided to reveal the twist twice for some reason. I get the lesson/takeaway of the film. Obsession can make you spiral into madness and lead to destruction. Was the plot really the best way to show that? Other than the writing, it has shots you would expect from an old film. I really love the one under the Golden Gate Bridge. The colors also look really nice and I thought the music was pretty decent.

Is this the greatest film of all time? Spare me. The plot is idiotic. Why does Judy go along with Scottie's creepy nonsense? Does she really think she can bail? Why doesn't she move from the hotel? Didn't Gavin give her a massive amount of money so she can fuck off from San Francisco forever? Is she trying to get caught? Is she fishing for a guy who can denounce her to the police? Why is she wearing the jewel from the crime scene? If so, why is she squirming when Scottie subjects her to his makeover? And what about the plan? How could he know that Scottie wouldn't make it up those stairs? Or what if Scottie waited until someone went upstairs, like a nun? Wouldn't that just invalidate the whole charade? How are they gonna get off the tower without being seen??? And Judy's still dressed as Madeleine, hair painted and everything! How could Scottie bring Madeleine's corpse up there, and if Scottie killed her there, why didn't the nuns, who came upstairs immediately when Scottie and Judy went there, hear Madeleine struggle? And, more than anything? Are we just gonna continue pretending the very visible threads Hitchcock pulls his characters through are psychologically real or in any way convincing? Or are we finally ready to admit they're just character contrivances some French critics in the 60s glazed over because they were 25-year-old dudes trying to prop up an unwieldy pseudo thesis who didn't give much of a fuck if women were written convincingly? Or if plots were written convincingly? Judy/Madeleine's character is utter nonsense from a psychological standpoint. Gavin's plot is unbelievable. Vertigo may look good, but for everyone still moping around the fact that Jeanne Dielman was pushed into being #1 on Sight & Sound should just go back and really look at the sham that is saying Vertigo is anything more than OK.
